stories.title: 🎶 Psalm 151
summaryBullets: I was small among my brothers and the youngest in my father’s house; I tended my father’s sheep. (1).
My hands made a harp; my fingers fashioned a lyre. (2).
And who will tell my Lord? The Lord himself; it is he who hears. (3).
It was he who sent his messenger and took me from my father’s sheep and anointed me with his anointing oil. (4).
My brothers were handsome and tall, but the Lord was not pleased with them. (5).
I went out to meet the foreigner, and he cursed me by his idols. (6).
But I drew his own sword; I beheaded him and removed disgrace from the people of Israel. (7).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 16:11–13 — David anointed by Samuel while keeping sheep.
1 Samuel 17:34–51 — David defeats Goliath with sling and sword.
Acts 13:22 — David described as a man after God’s heart, chosen to do His will.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מָשַׁח (mashach) — Greek: χρίω (chriō) — Aramaic/Syriac: משח (meshaḥ)
translationNotes.note: To pour oil on someone, setting them apart for God’s purpose; used for kings and priests.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָלַע (qalaʿ) — Greek: σφενδόνη (sphendonē) — Aramaic: קלעא (qelaʿa)
translationNotes.note: A weapon using a leather strap to hurl stones; David’s weapon against Goliath.

stories.keyTakeaway: Psalm 151, preserved in the Greek and other traditions, recounts David’s humble origins, his anointing, and his victory over Goliath as God’s chosen servant.
